source_text: Ὄνομα δὲ τῷ πάντων πατρὶ θετόν, ἀγεννήτῳ ὄντι, οὐκ ἔστιν· ᾧ γὰρ ἂν καὶ ὄνομά τι προσαγορεύεται, πρεσβύτερον ἔχει τὸν θέμενον τὸ ὄνομα. Τὸ δὲ πατὴρ καὶ θεὸς καὶ κτίστης καὶ κύριος καὶ δεσπότης οὐκ ὀνόματά ἐστιν, ἀλλ᾿ ἐκ τῶν εὐποιϊῶν καὶ τῶν ἔργων προσρήσεις. Ὁ δὲ υἱὸς ἐκείνου, ὁ μόνος λεγόμενος κυρίως υἱός, ὁ λόγος πρὸ τῶν ποιημάτων καὶ συνὼν καὶ γεννώμενος, ὅτε τὴν ἀρχὴν δι᾿ αὐτοῦ πάντα ἔκτισε καὶ ἐκόσμησε, Χριστὸς μὲν κατὰ τὸ κεχρῖσθαι καὶ κοσμῆσαι τὰ πάντα δι᾿ αὐτοῦ τὸν θεὸν λέγεται, ὄνομα καὶ αὐτὸ περιέχον ἄγνωστον σημασίαν, ὃν τρόπον καὶ τὸ θεὸς προσαγόρευμα οὐκ ὄνομά ἐστιν, ἀλλὰ πράγματος δυσεξηγήτου ἔμφυτος τῇ φύσει τῶν ἀνθρώπων δόξα. Ἰησοῦς δὲ καὶ ἀνθρώπου καὶ σωτῆρος ὄνομα καὶ σημασίαν ἔχει. Καὶ γὰρ καὶ ἄνθρωπος, ὡς προέφημεν, γέγονε κατὰ τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς βουλὴν ἀποκυηθεὶς ὑπὲρ τῶν πιστευόντων ἀνθρώπων καὶ ἐπὶ καταλύσει τῶν δαιμόνων· καὶ νῦν ἐκ τῶν ὑπ᾿ ὄψιν γινομένων μαθεῖν δύνασθε. Δαιμονιολήπτους γὰρ πολλοὺς κατὰ πάντα τὸν κόσμον καὶ ἐν τῇ ὑμετέρᾳ πόλει πολλοὶ τῶν ἡμετέρων ἀνθρώπων, τῶν Χριστιανῶν, ἐπορκίζοντες κατὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ σταυρωθέντος ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτου, ὑπὸ τῶν ἄλλων πάντων ἐπορκιστῶν καὶ ἐπᾳστῶν καὶ φαρμακευτῶν μὴ ἰαθέντας, ἰάσαντο καὶ ἔτι νῦν ἰῶνται, καταργοῦντες καὶ ἐκδιώκοντες τοὺς κατέχοντας τοὺς ἀνθρώπους δαίμονας.
thought_title: The names of the Father and the Son
orientation: Justin is explaining to the Roman Senate and people why the God Christians worship has no proper name, and what the titles Father, God, Creator, Lord, Master, Christ, and Jesus actually mean.
pass_a_gloss: A name for the Father of all, since he is unbegotten, there is not; for to whatever even some name is addressed, he has as older the one who set the name. But Father and God and Creator and Lord and Master are not names, but appellations from his good deeds and works. And the Son of that one, the only one properly called Son, the Word before the things made and being with him and being begotten, when in the beginning through him he created and ordered all things, is called Christ according to his being anointed and God's having ordered all things through him, a name itself also containing an unknown meaning, in the same way that the appellation God is not a name, but an innate opinion in the nature of humans about a thing hard to explain. But Jesus has the name and meaning of both a human being and a savior. For indeed he also became a human being, as we said before, according to the will of God and Father, having been born for the sake of believing humans and for the destruction of the demons; and now from the things happening under your eyes you can learn. For many demon-possessed people throughout the whole world and in your city, many of our people, the Christians, adjuring them by the name of Jesus Christ, the one crucified under Pontius Pilate, whom all the other exorcists and enchanters and sorcerers had not healed, healed them and still now heal them, nullifying and driving out the demons that possess the humans.

choices.term: ὄνομα δὲ τῷ πάντων πατρὶ θετόν, ἀγεννήτῳ ὄντι, οὐκ ἔστιν
choices.english: A name for the Father of all, since he is unbegotten, there is not
choices.why: Keeps the fronted dative and the causal force of the participle; the word order preserves Justin's emphasis that no name exists for the unbegotten Father.
rejected: The Father of all has no name, because he is unbegotten

choices.term: πρεσβύτερον ἔχει τὸν θέμενον τὸ ὄνομα
choices.english: he has as older the one who set the name
choices.why: Literal rendering of the comparative with the article, preserving the logical point that a name-giver must be prior to the one named.
rejected: the one who gave the name is older than he

choices.term: ἐκ τῶν εὐποιϊῶν καὶ τῶν ἔργων προσρήσεις
choices.english: appellations from his good deeds and works
choices.why: Keeps the plural 'appellations' and the source of the titles explicit, matching Justin's distinction between names and titles derived from actions.
rejected: titles based on his benefits and works

choices.term: ὁ λόγος πρὸ τῶν ποιημάτων καὶ συνὼν καὶ γεννώμενος
choices.english: the Word before the things made and being with him and being begotten
choices.why: Preserves the three participial phrases in their source order, showing the Word's pre-existence, coexistence, and generation.
rejected: the Word who existed before all creatures and was with him and was begotten

choices.term: ὄνομα καὶ αὐτὸ περιέχον ἄγνωστον σημασίαν
choices.english: a name itself also containing an unknown meaning
choices.why: Keeps the reflexive emphasis 'itself also' and the literal 'containing an unknown meaning,' which is Justin's point about the hidden significance of 'Christ.'
rejected: a name whose meaning is also unknown

choices.term: πράγματος δυσεξηγήτου ἔμφυτος τῇ φύσει τῶν ἀνθρώπων δόξα
choices.english: an innate opinion in the nature of humans about a thing hard to explain
choices.why: Literal rendering of the genitive 'of a thing hard to explain' and the adjective 'innate,' preserving Justin's philosophical claim about the natural human notion of God.
rejected: an implanted belief in human nature about something difficult to explain

pass_b_english: The Father of all has no name that anyone gave him, because he is unbegotten. For whoever is called by a name has someone older who gave him that name. But Father, God, Creator, Lord, and Master are not names; they are titles drawn from his good deeds and his works.

His Son is the only one properly called Son. He is the Word who existed before all created things, was with him, and was begotten when in the beginning God created and ordered all things through him. He is called Christ because God anointed him and through him ordered all things, and this name itself also contains an unknown meaning, just as the title God is not a name but an idea implanted in human nature about a reality that is hard to explain. Jesus, however, has the name and meaning of both a human being and a Savior.

For he also became a human being, as we said before, born according to the will of God the Father for the sake of those who believe in him and for the destruction of the demons. And now you can learn this from what happens before your eyes. Many of our people, the Christians, have exorcised in the name of Jesus Christ, who was crucified under Pontius Pilate, many demon-possessed people throughout the whole world and in your own city, people whom all the other exorcists, enchanters, and sorcerers had failed to heal. They have healed them and still heal them now, rendering powerless and driving out the demons that hold people captive.

last_rejected.source_quote: ἰάσαντο καὶ ἔτι νῦν ιῶνται, καταργοῦντες καὶ ἐκδιώκοντες τοὺς κατέχοντας τὸν δαίμονα
last_rejected.why: English leaves out the claim that Christians continue to heal and actively drive out demons, altering the sense of ongoing power.
last_rejected.fix: They have healed them and still heal them now, rendering powerless and driving out the demons that hold people captive.
last_rejected.ruling: English 'still heal them now' and 'rendering powerless and driving out' cover ἔτι νῦν ἰῶνται, καταργοῦντες καὶ ἐκδιώκοντες. No omission.

polish.changed: Clarified the subject of each clause, kept the theological terms consistent, and broke the long passage into three paragraphs where the thought turns from the Father's titles to the Son's identity and then to the evidence of exorcism.

notes.quote: His Son, the only one properly called Son, is the Word who existed before all created things
notes.why: Different English renderings of the same theological concept cause confusion.
notes.fix: Standardise as “the Word” throughout, noting “seed” as a metaphor.

polish.changed: Clarified the Son as the subject of the second paragraph, tightened sentence flow, and kept the demons consistently identified as the same beings throughout.

notes.why: Same beings called 'wicked demons,' 'demons,' and 'base demons' across sections; reader may wonder if these are different groups.
